messages:
Elaine (docs): FYI I opened a small PR with sample audit-log rows + a UX suggestion for the export flow. Need legal wording check and an eng sanity check on field names. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482
Sam (eng): Taking a look now. quick Q — are these samples intended for the CSV export or the JSONL export?
Elaine (docs): JSONL primarily but I added a CSV mapping table in the PR. Goal is to show a minimal, non-sensitive example rows that match the audit schema and make the export headers clear.
Priya (legal): Thanks — I skimmed. Please do not include any raw IPs or unmasked identifiers in examples. Prefer: "ip":"<redacted>" or a pseudonymized token. Also avoid saying "anonymized" unless it truly is irreversible.
Marco (platform): Agree with Priya. Also suggest we standardize on actor_id instead of user_id in examples to reflect our event model. If we keep a visible id, call it "hashed_actor_id" and show it's SHA256-like.
Sam (eng): Fine with actor_id. One small nit: the field we currently emit is "actor_type" (user, service). Can we surface that in the sample too so it's clear?
Elaine (docs): Good calls. I'll update. Proposed snippet (in the PR) is currently:```json
{"timestamp":"2024-04-04T12:00:00Z","actor_id":"hashed:8f14e45fceea167a5a36dedd4bea2543","actor_type":"user","event_type":"api_key.create","ip":"<redacted>","details":{"sdk":"python","cmd":"CreateKey"}}
```
Priya (legal): That looks much better. Two phrasing suggestions for the docs copy: 1) Replace "PII removed" with "pseudonymized or redacted"; 2) Add a short note under the sample: "Fields containing sensitive identifiers are redacted or pseudonymized in examples."
Sam (eng): For clarity add "kms_key_id" as an example field and mark it as optional in the sample so prod teams know it's present but not required.
Elaine (docs): Updated PR text to include your points and inserted a table row showing CSV column -> JSON path mapping. Also pushed the snippet change.
lint-bot: docs lint check — 1 warning in docs/export.md: sample-json-literal should be fenced with triple backticks + json language.
Elaine (docs): Oops, thanks lint-bot. Fixed the fencing and rebased. I'll @Sam and @Priya again once CI is green and request an explicit legal approval comment so we have a trace.
Marco (platform): Quick follow-up: for the UX guidance, should the export include a metadata row with export_time and requested_by? That helps auditability for customers. If we add that, include an example header in the CSV and a top-level object for JSONL.
Priya (legal): That's useful. If we include requested_by in the sample, ensure the docs say it will be pseudonymized for public examples and may include real IDs in customer exports depending on their settings.
Sam (eng): Sounds good. I'll run the PR locally to check the CSV mapping table renders well and flag any schema mismatches.
Elaine (docs): Thanks everyone — updated PR and requested reviews: @Sam @Priya @Marco. Will merge after legal ACK and lint/CI pass. :thumbsup:
